incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: Attacker compromised the exchange and drained funds across multiple wallets; the precise intrusion method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Up to $6.3 billion in funds was affected in what is being called the largest crypto heist on record; roughly $1.2-3 billion in USDT and ETH escaped recovery despite partial freezes by Tether and Circle.

incidents.victim: Sony (So-net internet service provider)
incidents.vector: Not disclosed by the company.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to 2.58 million So-net customers was stolen.

incidents.victim: GMO (Onamae Desktop Cloud / FX trading service)
incidents.vector: Hackers accessed GMO's Onamae Desktop Cloud service hosting its FX foreign-exchange trading platform.
incidents.impact: Attackers demanded a $50 million ransom and leaked stolen data on the dark web after GMO refused to pay; GMO is now offering a $1 million reward for information leading to the hackers.

incidents.victim: Vapor Panda campaign targets: foreign ministries, defense/intelligence agencies, and 19 U.S. pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear and financial-sector organizations across 14 countries
incidents.vector: Threat actor paired the ARTEX agentic AI penetration-testing framework with the DeepSeek LLM to run autonomous intrusions at machine speed, issuing requests as often as every 10 seconds across many targets concurrently.
incidents.impact: Compromised roughly 140 of 200+ targeted organizations in 14 countries within 11 days, including a European country's presidency and prime minister's office; the campaign remains active and growing.

incidents.victim: Cursor (Claude Code VS Code Marketplace extension users)
incidents.vector: Attacker compromised the Cursor Marketplace publishing pipeline and swapped the official Claude Code extension for a trojanized version containing a 66-line SSH-backdoor loader.
incidents.impact: The malicious version was live for roughly 11 hours and reached up to 5,000 users; it attempted to install an attacker SSH key and reverse tunnel and exfiltrated host reconnaissance data, though admin-privilege requirements blocked most SSH access attempts.

incidents.victim: Revolve
incidents.vector: Threat actors used automated means to access multiple company systems and harvest saved payment card data.
incidents.impact: Names, contact information, and payment card numbers/expiration dates were stolen for customers with saved payment info; at least 128,500+ individuals have been notified across Texas, Vermont and Massachusetts.

incidents.victim: Polymarket (via third-party provider DebugBear)
incidents.vector: Attacker compromised third-party website-performance provider DebugBear and injected wallet-draining JavaScript into sites embedding its code.
incidents.impact: More than $2.1 million in cryptocurrency was siphoned from Polymarket users before trading was halted; Polymarket is reimbursing all affected traders.

incidents.victim: Japan Airlines (via a passenger-management supplier)
incidents.vector: A hack of one of JAL's passenger-management suppliers exposed traveler data.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 90,000 travelers was exposed.

incidents.victim: Belgian Ministry of Finance (MyMinfin tax portal)
incidents.vector: Not disclosed; an intrusion was detected that forced the portal offline.
incidents.impact: Belgium's national tax-filing portal was taken offline for days just before the annual filing deadline, which was extended to November 16.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security
incidents.vector: Hacktivist group "Department of Peace" obtained data from a DHS Okta single sign-on database.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 41,000 DHS employees — mostly ICE and CBP staff — was leaked, with records dating back to 2011.

incidents.victim: Government of Moldova
incidents.vector: Hackers breached government networks and began extracting data; IT staff detected the exfiltration in progress.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly one-third of Moldova's population was exposed; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers (2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants) and broader targets in enterprise software, industrial automation, semiconductor and telecom sectors in the US/Europe
incidents.vector: Threat actor Storm-0940 (overlapping with GTIG's UNC7228) compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup application credentials, then used the ARTEX agentic AI pentesting framework to mass-automate sign-in attempts at up to 2,900/minute against downstream Microsoft 365 tenants.
incidents.impact: Attempted access against more than 2,250 customer tenants, achieving privileged cloud persistence at multiple organizations within three hours; ConnectWise suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security and Cloud Management services.

incidents.victim: ~600 organizations across the Americas, Europe, and Australia in multiple critical infrastructure sectors
incidents.vector: SafePay actors gain access via compromised credentials and known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN devices, then use legitimate IT tools to move laterally and disable backups before exfiltrating data and deploying ransomware.
incidents.impact: One of the most active ransomware groups of 2026, with roughly 600 confirmed victims; the group also uses double-extortion tactics including direct phone calls threatening to publish stolen data.

incidents.victim: 15 Argentina-based healthcare organizations
incidents.vector: A Spanish/English-speaking operator ran a custom autonomous pentesting harness built on Claude Code, using a dual-agent "Supervisor/Executor" architecture derived from the open-source PentestGPT project.
incidents.impact: Compromised at least 15 Argentina-based healthcare entities, exfiltrating credentials and medical records from at least one victim.

incidents.victim: Government entities in two countries and private-sector organizations in Brazil and the U.S. (biotech, healthcare, food & beverage, retail, technology, travel)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking operator accessed Claude models via a China-based AI proxy service and built two custom agentic pentesting harnesses granting varying levels of autonomy for reconnaissance, lateral movement and privilege escalation.
incidents.impact: Compromised government entities in two countries and private-sector targets across Brazil and the U.S. spanning six industries.

incidents.victim: A U.S.-based CRM vendor and several private-sector SaaS/data-center entities in Russia, Kyrgyzstan, and the U.S.
incidents.vector: A group of Russian-speaking individuals used a single custom Claude Code slash command to run a seven-step autonomous workflow granting near-total autonomy in exploitation, with explicit exfiltration instructions.
incidents.impact: Exfiltrated corporate client data from a U.S.-based customer relationship management vendor and compromised multiple SaaS and data-center entities plus one additional government domain.

incidents.victim: Indonesian government domains, one additional government domain, and several private-sector entities
incidents.vector: A low-sophistication Indonesian-speaking operator used 819 publicly sourced GitHub "skills" without orchestration, directly instructing Claude Code to compromise targets with minimal operator intervention.
incidents.impact: Compromised several Indonesian government domains, one additional government domain, and multiple private-sector entities despite the operator's limited grasp of security fundamentals.

incidents.victim: John Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins (via a third-party vendor), and roughly 100 global e-commerce/payment sites
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking attacker used the AI-driven penetration-testing tool Cairn to automate vulnerability discovery (SQL injection, insecure deserialization, auth bypass) and deploy web shells across exposed e-commerce and payment infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Compromised roughly 100 sites globally with at least one confirmed web shell install; John Deere and SharkNinja each confirmed and contained incidents, while Cummins is investigating a compromise of a third-party vendor's website.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited (Certificate Authority)
incidents.vector: Eight eMudhra emSign G3 intermediate CA private keys were generated with insufficient cryptographic randomness, allowing the keys to be mathematically derived from their public certificates.
incidents.impact: The weak keys could let third parties forge trusted TLS and code-signing certificates to conduct man-in-the-middle interception or malware impersonation; major browser and OS vendors revoked trust in the affected roots and eMudhra revoked the certificates.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, hospitality, manufacturing, government, transportation and utilities sectors
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators exploited the PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257) to gain VPN access, then pivoted to vCenter/ESXi to disable security controls and perform offline credential dumping against domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Confirmed exploitation across numerous industries since June 2026; the pivot to the virtualization layer bypasses in-guest EDR, representing a sophisticated path to domain-wide credentials ahead of ransomware deployment.

incidents.victim: Multiple sectors worldwide, including education, financial services, healthcare, manufacturing and government
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators including Qilin, Inc, and Settra exploited the PHP2Shell remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-109618/109619) to gain initial footholds on internet-facing PHP servers.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed across many sectors since the vulnerabilities' disclosure; millions of exposed PHP servers running end-of-life versions remain unpatched, extending the exposure window.

incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education (Florida Student Financial Aid website)
incidents.vector: An unauthorized party gained access to a system or database containing the financial-aid site's customer information.
incidents.impact: Social Security numbers, addresses, and other PII of nearly 4.9 million financial-aid applicants were exposed; the site was taken offline.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime, and global shipping companies (via IT provider CyberLogitec)
incidents.vector: Ransomware and data-extortion group "n0n" compromised a maritime IT services provider, CyberLogitec, and pivoted downstream into customer networks.
incidents.impact: More than 40 victims were listed on the group's dark web leak site; their final payment deadline expired October 19, 2026.

incidents.victim: Federal Bureau of Investigation (job applicant site apply.fbijobs.gov)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters hackers breached the FBI's job application website and exfiltrated personnel records.
incidents.impact: Stolen data reportedly includes Social Security numbers, medical/psychological records, and home addresses for more than 5,000 FBI personnel; the group has threatened to publish the files, and the investigation has led to related arrests.

incidents.victim: Zenith Technology
incidents.vector: Zawoo ransomware attack hit the clinical-trial and analytical-laboratory services provider.
incidents.impact: Delayed lab work and coronial autopsy investigations across New Zealand for patients and the Ministry of Justice.
